title: W0 CENSUS FREEZE: the authorized codification ledger, one row per norm
description: The epic's fixed target, and the reason every later task can be checked mechanically. Convert the context-scout's census (.harness/context-brief-codification.md sections 1.1-1.7) into an AUTHORIZED LEDGER at docs/precedent-research/codification-ledger.md: exactly which norms mint records, which are deliberately left uncodified and why, and the expected census arithmetic per wave. Every later publish task publishes THIS ledger and nothing else; every verify task compares the live registry census against it. That comparison is the only instrument in this system that can catch a duplicate record, because publish is NOT idempotent (allocate_next_id is max+1 with no duplicate-content check, .harness/bin/precedent.py:683-696) and conflicts is blind to a perfect clone BY DESIGN (detector 1 skips identical-ratio pairs, .harness/bin/precedent.py:2074). That pair of gaps is how PR-030 and PR-031 were minted; PR-032's ratio is the standing record of it. You draft no ratios, and you publish nothing.
acceptance_criteria: OWNS EXACTLY docs/precedent-research/codification-ledger.md (NEW file). MUST NOT write anything under .harness/, MUST NOT run precedent.py publish, MUST NOT edit ORCHESTRATION.md, PRECEDENT.md, INTERPRETIVE-CODE.md, AGENTS.md, claude.md, gemini.md, .harness/state.json or any test file. docs/ is gitignored (.gitignore:33), so the ledger ships operator-local: no record may ever cite it by path (it would dangle for every clone). Every row's anchor token is decision:T-377#<anchor>, matching the shipped grammar ^decision:T-\d{3,}#[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$ (.harness/bin/precedent.py DECISION_RE).

ONE ROW PER NORM, no column left blank: row id (CD-NN) | norm | wave 1|2|3 | EVERY prose home (repo-relative path plus section heading; a line range only where the home is line-addressable) | primary home | disposition MINT / ALREADY-CODIFIED PR-NNN / NOT-CODIFIED plus reason | authority_tier | exact tier_evidence tokens | operation type and subtype | declared_width | sources tokens | validity_conditions entries | subject slug | title with its character count.

THE CLI'S REFUSAL SURFACE IS THE SPEC, AND YOU REPLAY IT RATHER THAN ASSUME IT: run python3 .harness/bin/precedent.py publish --help and quote the flag list. Every row must satisfy: title <= 80 characters (refusal message 'title exceeds 80 chars (SDR-17.2)'); subject matching ^[a-z0-9-]+$; tier in 1..4 carrying the tier_evidence KIND the PRECEDENT.md section-3 table demands (tier 1: at least one event: or T-NNN token; tier 2: at least one P-NNN token; tiers 3 and 4: at least one T-NNN token naming the issuing task); scope_conditions, revisit_trigger and validity_conditions all non-empty at tiers 1-3; sources non-empty always; --code-version v1 (INTERPRETIVE-CODE.md's 'Version: v1' line); operation determination with a null subtype unless a relation forces otherwise. A row the CLI would refuse is a LEDGER defect, not a worker problem.

THE THREE WAVES ARE CD7's AND ARE NOT YOURS TO RE-CUT. Wave 1: the eight ORCHESTRATION.md section-3 invariant rows (lines 92-103) plus the standing-force P-numbers in state.json evolution.accepted_mutations. Wave 2: the audit-born norms - F6, U2 and U4 as ORCHESTRATION.md rules; F1, U1 and U3 against their ACTUAL homes with their narrower reach stated. They are not a peer set and a ledger that flattens them is a defect. Wave 3: the state.json normative structures - human_gates.require_human_approval_for, limits, cost_policy.frontier_budget and its seven rules (with the below-band finding noted), protected_paths. State per row why it sits in its wave.

CROSS-WAVE AND CROSS-HOME DUPLICATE RESOLUTION - the row-level defense against minting one norm twice. Every norm gets exactly ONE minting row; any second appearance is marked SUBSUMED-BY CD-NN. Resolve at minimum these by name: P-024 versus cost_policy rule 4; P-030 versus cost_policy rule 1 and frontier_budget; P-020 versus cost_policy rule 3; P-029 versus protected_paths; the 'bounded everything' invariant row versus limits.*; the 'human gates' invariant row versus human_gates.require_human_approval_for; the 'producer != approver' invariant row versus P-009 and its six prose homes. CD8: a double-homed norm gets ONE record citing every home and naming which is primary.

ORCH-HOME FLAG, and the mechanical rule that follows from it: mark every row whose norm has an ORCHESTRATION.md home. An ORCH-HOME row MUST sit in wave 1 or wave 2, because the backlink task T-386 runs after wave 2 and must be able to mark 100 percent of ORCH-HOME rows. A wave-3 row carrying an ORCHESTRATION.md home is a ledger defect: reassign it, or state explicitly why no marker is owed.

These four are the reopen rule (P-023), P-025, P-026 and F6; NONE may be re-minted. Then run python3 .harness/bin/precedent.py list --json and prove no proposed subject slug collides with any of the 34 existing subjects - paste the comparison, do not assert it.

PR-001's dangling P-023 token must still be reported by conflicts when this epic ends; a ledger designed to silence it is an automatic REJECT.

The word 'backfill' must not appear in their rows - they are a complete and correct historical record already. Recorded default you may overrule with reasoning: ONE consolidated record for both.

CD5 - ANTI-COMPLETIONISM IS A COLUMN, NOT A MOOD: every census item the scout found either MINTs or appears in the NOT-CODIFIED column WITH ITS REASON, so the boundary is chosen rather than accidental. Recorded default you may overrule with reasoning: the entangled point-fix P-numbers (P-002, P-005, P-006, P-007, P-008, P-011, P-012, P-013) do not mint individually, because their normative content is inseparable from the bug they fixed. If you mint the consolidated observability-theme record the scout suggests, its ratio must state the generalizable rule and not the bug story, and it must name its member P-numbers in tier_evidence.

CD6 - ANCHORING TO VERIFIABLE FACTS: every row's tier_evidence names a fact a CLI or git can check (the accepted_mutations entry, the issuing T-NNN, an events.jsonl timestamp, the commit that introduced the norm, the audit file section). A row with no verifiable anchor carries a NO-VERIFIABLE-ANCHOR note and takes the tier its evidence supports, not the tier tradition suggests. This is the partial TIER-EVIDENCE-A repair and the join audits it.
